messages.author: bb37bae01bd466aa
messages.subject: Multiple signals at same time
parts:
Hi again,

Upon a resource is released, I send a signal which is arrival-specific that triggers the next arrival (the one with attribute 'id' equal to optIdRegion1) to seize the resource. This works perfectly when arrivals release the resources one by one. However, when multiple resources are released simultaniously, the signal is send multiple times causing the arrival to rerun through my trajectory as many times as there were signals sent. 

However, I only want one signal to be sent at that particular moment in time as job24 only has to pass through the trajectory once. How can I make sure the signal is only sent once?




pickingRegion1Trajectory <- trajectory("Picking Process") %>%
  untrap(function() set_signal()) %>%
  log_("Now in picking traject") %>%
  timeout(function() remove_job_from_regionqueu1()) %>%
  seize("pickOperatorRegion1") %>%
  timeout(function() decrease_picker_available_region1()) %>%
  timeout_from_attribute("historicalPickingTime") %>%
  timeout(function() find_opt_id_region1()) %>%
  timeout(function() increase_picker_available_region1()) %>%
  release("pickOperatorRegion1") %>%
  send(function() paste("Request for job with id", optIdRegion1)) %>%
  timeout(function() set_optIdRegion1_to_NULL()) %>%


env %>% 
add_resource("pickOperatorRegion1", 3, 0)

env %>% run(700) %>%
  now()

And I encounter the following problem:


















Job 0, 8 and 16, together make pool 1. And, job 28, 29 and 30 together make pool 2. Job 16 is the last job of pool 1 and should trigger job 0 and job 8 to go to the workcenter4CompletePoolStingrayTrajectory. 


The problem is that when job 30 arrives it directly joins workcenter4CompletePoolStingrayTrajectory (before job 0 and 8). How can I make sure that first the join() in the trap is executed by job 16 before a new signal is sent (as job 30 does). That is, how can I make sure that job 0 and 8 are released from wait() and join the trajectory before job 30 sends a signal? 

When the moment of job arrival differs per job, it works perfectly fine. The problem only occurs when two arrivals simultaniously arrive.

Thanks!

On Wed, 15 Apr 2020 at 15:34, Eras <j.e...@student.tue.nl> wrote:

>
> workcenter4CompletePoolStingrayTrajectory <- trajectory("Pool is completed, trigger generator") %>%
> timeout(function() get_pool_attributes()) %>%

Note that this is redundant. If get_pool_attributes is already a
function that doesn't need any input argument, then you can just
write:

timeout(get_pool_attributes)

> branch(function() determine_pool_generator(),

The same applies here.

> continue=c(TRUE, TRUE),
> trajectory() %>% log_("Leaving") %>% leave(1),
> trajectory() %>% activate("MultiManualSortingPool") %>% log_("Activated pool generator, now leaving") %>% leave(1))
>
>
> workcenter4IncompletePoolStingrayTrajectory <- trajectory("Check if job completes a pool") %>%
> log_("Now in incomplete pool trajectory wc4") %>%
> branch(function() determine_if_pool_complete_workcenter4(),
And the same applies here.

> continue=c(TRUE, TRUE),
> trajectory() %>% log_("I completed a pool!") %>% send(function() paste("Request for jobs with poolID", get_attribute(env, "poolId"))) %>% join(workcenter4CompletePoolStingrayTrajectory),
> trajectory() %>% trap(function() set_pool_signal(),
> trajectory() %>% log_("Got a signal!")
> %>% join(workcenter4CompletePoolStingrayTrajectory), interruptible=FALSE)
> %>% wait())
>
> And I encounter the following problem:

The error means that the 'option' function should return a single
value, and it's not returning anything, probably NULL (extent=0).

> Job 0, 8 and 16, together make pool 1. And, job 28, 29 and 30 together make pool 2. Job 16 is the last job of pool 1 and should trigger job 0 and job 8 to go to the workcenter4CompletePoolStingrayTrajectory.
>
>
> The problem is that when job 30 arrives it directly joins workcenter4CompletePoolStingrayTrajectory (before job 0 and 8). How can I make sure that first the join() in the trap is executed by job 16 before a new signal is sent (as job 30 does). That is, how can I make sure that job 0 and 8 are released from wait() and join the trajectory before job 30 sends a signal?

Simultaneous events are tricky. There's a section in the JSS paper
discussing this. E.g., the send() activity always takes precedence,
because in most use cases this is the best option. On the other hand,
a timeout has the minimum priority if several events are scheduled at
the same time, so you could try adding a timeout(0) before the send()
activity (please, update to version 4.4.1, already on CRAN, before
trying this, because it has a bug fix about this).
> When the moment of job arrival differs per job, it works perfectly fine. The problem only occurs when two arrivals simultaniously arrive.

Yeap, as I said, it's tricky. But in real world, simultaneous events
are quite rare. Using always continuous random distributions for
arrivals and service times minimizes these kind of problems.

--
Iñaki Úcar
